name: Calculus
description: Authored practice spanning the supplied 24-lecture syllabus: functions, limits, differentiation, integration, sequences, series, complex numbers and multivariable calculus. Problems are independent teaching exercises, not reproduced examination questions.
limitations: Scope follows the supplied local lecture transcription and course overview, not a live 2026-27 syllabus verification. Historical assessment rules are deliberately omitted.

Lecture PDFs are predominantly image-based. Text extraction was attempted for all 24; only representative pages were visually inspected. The supplied Lectures.md transcription is the main content source and contains OCR errors; formulas here were independently reconstructed.
The supplementary formula sheet contains errors, including the complex exponential identity and a geometric-series interval. It is not treated as authoritative.
Notes and selected 2023 examination PDFs were sampled for scope and style; the complete textbook, all examinations, recordings and linked interactive videos were not reviewed.
Source references identify conceptual grounding, not an original exercise number or an official answer key. Every exercise here is newly authored.
Open responses require human self-review against explanations and rubrics and must never be automatically graded. This portable data file has no application integration or grading implementation.

name: Human Computer Interaction and AI-Assisted Prototyping
description: Archive-grounded preparation in user-centred requirements, interaction design, prototyping and evaluation, with separately labelled legacy web implementation practice. The new Generative-AI prototyping component is a documented source gap, not an invented tool syllabus.
limitations: The supplied README and HCIAP instructions describe a new first-year course formally replacing CSE1500 WDT. The CSE3500 HCI material is subject-matter background, not evidence that the entire former third-year elective survives.

The archive provides no teaching material, approved-tool list, prompting workflow, assessment rubric or worked project for the new Generative-AI-assisted prototyping component. The final topic applies inherited HCI methods to project planning and explicitly records this gap; it does not teach or certify unsupported GenAI techniques.

HTML/CSS, JavaScript, REST, Node/Express, React and WebSockets are optional predecessor implementation background. Their presence, including old WDT texts relabelled CSE12B, does not establish that they are on the new syllabus.

Old HCI and WDT marks, dates, pass rules and exam formats are not transferred to CSE12B. Statistical evaluation and adaptive-interface theory are included as legacy extensions with unconfirmed new-course depth.
Design and evaluation tasks use open rubrics. Alternative defensible answers are expected; the material does not claim objective automatic grading of designs, usability or research conclusions.

All 52 supplied non-hidden PDF/Markdown files were inventoried and text-extracted; document-level contents and relevant course passages were inspected. The 674-page textbook was consulted selectively, not read cover to cover. Not every illustration or historical solution was independently verified.

Lessons and exercises are original adaptations, not copied exam questions. Supplied summaries contain OCR errors, broad claims and speculation; examples avoid relying on disputed historical technical claims or presenting them as current standards.

topics.name: Web prototype foundations: HTTP, HTML, CSS and JavaScript
Prototype-and-evaluation project: evidence and source gaps

name: Data Management
description: Source-grounded preparation covering data modelling, relational querying, database access and the inherited database-systems material. Introductory WDT DB foundations precede explicitly labelled IDM extensions. This is an archive-based study curriculum, not a verified official 2026-27 syllabus.
limitations: The supplied README and DM instructions describe CSE12C as a new 5 EC merger. They explicitly warn that the combined predecessor content is broader than the new course. No complete official CSE12C teaching schedule or assessment specification is supplied.

Storage, multidimensional indexing, query-optimization internals, concurrency protocols, recovery and distributed systems are retained as labelled legacy IDM extensions. Their inclusion here does not establish that they are examinable.

URIs/URLs are explicitly mentioned in the supplied new-course description. The concrete inherited material teaches JDBC connection URLs and persistence APIs; this does not establish a full REST syllabus.

All SQL and schema-design submissions are open reasoning exercises with rubrics. No SQL is executed, and no string comparison is presented as semantic SQL grading. SQL examples use conventional relational/PostgreSQL-style syntax; engine-specific behaviour is stated when needed.

Sources include legacy exams, student notes, textbook transcriptions and duplicated bundles. Some dates, labels and example solutions conflict. New exercises are original and self-contained; historical marks, deadlines, pass thresholds and permitted aids are not carried forward.

All 77 supplied non-hidden PDF/Markdown files were inventoried and text-extracted; document-level contents and course-relevant passages were inspected. Large textbooks were consulted selectively, not read cover to cover. Image-only SQL sheets were visually inspected. Not every diagram or historical worked answer was independently verified.

topics.name: Database access, persistence and resource identifiers
Recovery, distributed commit and alternative models

name: Linear Algebra
description: Authored computational and reasoning practice across the supplied lecture syllabus, from linear systems and transformations to eigenstructure, discrete dynamics, orthogonality, least squares and the spectral theorem. Matrices are written as lists of rows and vectors as coordinate tuples; scalars are real unless a problem explicitly uses complex numbers.
limitations: Scope follows the supplied local lecture transcription and overview, not a live verification of the 2026-27 syllabus. Historical assessment and grading rules vary between supplied documents and are omitted.

Text extraction was attempted for all 21 lecture PDFs, which are predominantly image-based. Only representative PDF pages were visually sampled; the supplied Lectures.md transcription is the main content source and can contain OCR errors.
Selected 2023 exam solutions and supplementary notes were sampled, not the complete examination archive or textbook. Video recordings and external links were not reviewed.

QR factorization is explicitly excluded in the supplied lecture 18 programme and is not taught here. This is a full lecture-theme practice set, not a claim to reproduce every textbook section or official exercise.
Problems and explanations are newly authored. Source links identify conceptual grounding rather than official question provenance or an official marking scheme.
Open responses are ungraded and require human review using their rubrics. The portable file does not integrate with the application or implement a grader.

topics.name: Linear systems, echelon forms and spans

name: Software Design and Engineering
description: An integrated study curriculum across the supplied software engineering and testing archive: requirements, modeling, architecture, design, teamwork and evolution, systematic testing, delivery, and responsible evaluation of development tools. Original cases connect design decisions with observable quality.
limitations: CSE13B is a merged course. This curriculum covers the supplied CSE2115 SEM and CSE1110 SQT predecessor material; it does not claim a verified final CSE13B syllabus or examination specification.

The supplied README explicitly leaves merged-course assessment, oral-presentation requirements and depth of inherited advanced topics unconfirmed. Communication practice is included as a useful inherited skill, not a mandatory CSE13B assessment.

Past SEM exams span older formats and are used for topic/problem-style evidence only. SQT exams and exercises are supplied mainly as Markdown WebLab exports; their copied solutions are not treated as authoritative new marking schemes.

All problems and lesson prose are newly authored. Open design, diagrams, proofs and test/code-writing responses are ungraded and require rubric-based self or instructor review; no code or arbitrary user input is executed.
PDF locators use one-based physical pages. Text extraction, content sampling and selected visual checks were used; not every source page was visually reviewed.

Historical tool names, organizational examples and AI claims in source slides are context, not verified current recommendations. The material teaches durable reasoning rather than current product capabilities.

topics.name: Delivery, observability and operation at scale
Coverage, MC/DC, mutation and regression selection
Test doubles and design for testability

name: Algorithms and Data Structures
description: A complete study path through the supplied CSE13C syllabus: algorithm reasoning, complexity, linear containers, trees, sorting and selection, maps, balanced search trees, and graph algorithms. Original worked examples and practice connect implementation decisions to correctness and cost.
limitations: Based on the supplied local course archive, including legacy CSE1305 material; this is a study curriculum, not an official assessment specification.
Exercises are original teaching problems aligned with the sources, not transcriptions of exam questions or official marking schemes.
Open proofs, designs and Java/pseudocode responses require self or instructor review using their rubrics. No code is executed and no compilation or implementation-exam equivalence is claimed.
PDF page references are one-based physical PDF pages. Some lecture filenames misdescribe their contents; locators identify the actual relevant sections.
Textbook coverage is bounded to the sections listed in the supplied course outline; unrelated textbook chapters are not additional syllabus requirements.

topics.name: Priority queues, heaps and adaptable entries
Merge sort, quicksort and comparison lower bounds
Key-based sorting, selection and algorithm design
Maps, hashing, sets and sorted maps
Binary search trees and ordered operations
Graph representations, DFS, BFS and DAGs
Shortest paths and minimum spanning trees

name: Probability Theory and Statistics
description: A source-grounded path from probability models and random variables to estimation, confidence intervals, regression and responsible hypothesis testing, with original worked examples and practice.
limitations: Based on the supplied course archive, including older CSE1210 materials; this is not a statement of current examination rules.
Exercises are newly authored practice, not official past-exam questions or a prediction of exam coverage. Open exercises require self-review against the rubric and are ungraded.
Most lecture PDFs are image-based. Their supplied transcription was cross-checked against sampled rendered slides and the textbook; not every slide received visual review.
Normal approximations, distribution parameterizations, quantile conventions and independence assumptions are stated where used. N(mu, sigma^2) always uses variance as its second parameter.

Bootstrap and variance tests extend the main lecture sequence using the supplied book/course overview. No external Grasple tasks, recording videos or unavailable computer-assignment datasets are reproduced.

topics.name: Estimation, bias and mean squared error
Sums, generating functions and Gaussian vectors
Comparisons, multiple testing and study design

name: Computer Networks
description: Understand and trace a network from framing and medium access through IP, transport, security and distributed applications, using original calculations and protocol scenarios grounded in the supplied course archive.
limitations: Based on supplied CSE14B/CSE1405 teaching materials, not current product recommendations or examination regulations.
All exercises are newly authored practice. Open responses are ungraded and require review against their rubrics.
Historical Ethernet, TCP Tahoe/Reno, simplified handshakes and toy cryptography are explicitly teaching models, not claims about every deployed implementation.
No packet captures, physical labs, external recordings or live network experiments were run. Scenario traces are analytical exercises.

Source PDFs were text-inspected with sampled visual checks, not exhaustively reviewed diagram by diagram. Student summaries were treated as secondary and corrected where they conflict with precise protocol reasoning.

Decimal network rates use 1000-based prefixes; byte/bit conversions and omitted overhead are stated in calculation prompts. Cryptographic examples with tiny keys or toy ciphers are for arithmetic only.

topics.name: Wireless access, learning switches and spanning trees
UDP, TCP sequencing and connection state
Flow control, congestion and transport limits
